about: The first prayer of the Canon. Through Jesus Christ, the priest asks the Father to accept the offerings and to grant the Church peace, protection, unity and governance. The missal leaves a slot here for the reigning Pope and the local bishop, named with all who keep the Catholic faith.

seg.nr: After the Preface the priest spreads his hands, raises them slightly and joins them, lifts his eyes to heaven and lowers them at once, then bows low before the altar and rests his hands upon it.

seg.tr: Therefore, most merciful Father, through Jesus Christ, Your Son, our Lord, we humbly pray and beseech You

seg.nr: The priest kisses the altar and joins his hands before his breast.
The priest makes three signs of the cross over the Host and the chalice together.

seg.tr: these gifts, these offerings, these holy, undefiled sacrifices.

seg.nr: The priest spreads his hands and goes on.

seg.tr: We offer them to You above all for Your holy Catholic Church. Graciously grant her peace, preserve her, unite her, and govern her throughout the world,

ex.w030: In primis is a fixed adverbial phrase meaning “first of all”.
ex.w048: The whole phrase means the whole world.

seg.tr: together with Your servant our Pope and our Bishop, and all those who are orthodox in belief and uphold the Catholic and Apostolic faith.

ex.w057: The Missal prints “N.” after “Antístite nostro”: each place names its own bishop here.
